name: Conor Pedroche

hobbies.name: Balisong flipping
paragraphs: I enjoy balisong flipping. A balisong, also called a butterfly knife, has two handles that rotate around the blade. Flipping involves learning tricks and connecting those movements into sequences.

hobbies.name: Speedcubing
paragraphs: Speedcubing is solving a Rubik’s Cube as quickly as you can. My fastest solve was 13 seconds, though that was a while ago.
I’ve recently gotten back into it and am practicing to get close to that time again.

hobbies.name: Basketball
paragraphs: I also like playing basketball. It’s another way I enjoy spending time away from my desk.

experience.label: Hardware & technical support
experience.summary: Building custom gaming PCs around each customer's budget, performance goals, and preferences.
points: Designed, built, and optimized custom gaming PCs for 30+ customers, balancing performance, compatibility, power requirements, thermals, and budget.
Researched and compared CPUs, GPUs, PSUs, cooling systems, and other components using PCPartPicker.
Diagnosed POST errors, boot loops, overheating, memory instability, driver conflicts, system crashes, freezing, and blue-screen errors through component isolation and stress testing.
Optimized systems through cable management, cooling solutions, BIOS/UEFI configuration, and software configuration.

experience.label: Teaching & mentorship
experience.summary: Helping students navigate demanding coursework and the next step after high school.
points: Tutored junior AVID students in AP U.S. History, AP English Language and Composition, and Precalculus.
Mentored students on succeeding in future AP courses: English Literature and Composition, Government, Macroeconomics, Calculus AB, Physics 1, and Environmental Science.
Guided students through college applications and scholarships, sharing strategies from personal experience.

experience.label: Engineering leadership
experience.summary: Making engineering tangible through hands-on projects and a welcoming STEM community.
points: Led monthly STEM meetings and 11 hands-on engineering projects, creating technical presentations, organizing competitive activities, and guiding teams through planning, design, testing, and final builds.
Recruited and retained 20+ new members through outreach to underrepresented students, building collaboration, technical and critical thinking, and team design skills.
Collaborated with Cal Poly students to organize STEM workshops and campus visits for local high school students.

experience.organization: UC Santa Barbara · Summer Research Academies
experience.label: Computational social science
experience.summary: Investigating how media outlet reputation shapes political bias in online audience reactions.
points: Collected and processed 1,802 Reddit discussion threads, 18,020 comments, and 101 news outlets using the Reddit API, Selenium, and Python, linking sources, threads, and audience responses.
Automated collection of follower data from X (Twitter) to measure media outlet reputation and integrated it into a structured dataset.
Applied VADER sentiment analysis, correlation analysis, and multiple linear regression to study media reputation, article tone, political topics, and audience responses.

Co-authored and presented a research paper at the Capstone Seminar. The analysis found a statistically significant relationship between media reputation and audience political bias, with government policy and elections showing the strongest effects.

projects.name: Sourcecado
projects.headline: An AI workflow that can pick up where it left off.
projects.description: A local-first AI desktop application built with FastAPI, WebSockets, React, TypeScript, Tauri, and SQLite. The engineering focus: recover interrupted work reliably and keep external actions tied to explicit approval.

points.title: Recover without repeating
points.text: Restores saved responses and resumes eligible interrupted agent runs under their original IDs. Idempotent processing prevents duplicate messages and external actions.

points.title: Keep approvals meaningful
points.text: Centralized approval validation binds external actions to verified recipients and reviewed message content. Enrichment requests and API entry points preserve authorization.

points.title: Test the failure paths
points.text: 228 pytest and 35 Vitest tests for the Gmail connection feature cover migrations, retries, message attribution, and failure recovery.

projects.name: Campus Event Finder
projects.headline: A campus event search tool for students.
projects.description: A full-stack application that helps students discover campus events by date, category, and location, with a Flask REST API and persistent SQLite storage.

points.title: Find the right event
points.text: Search and filter campus events by date, category, and location on campus.

points.title: Build the complete workflow
points.text: Designed REST endpoints for event creation, retrieval, filtering, and deletion, backed by SQLite.

points.title: Protect the boundaries
points.text: Implemented user authentication and input validation to protect accounts and prevent invalid event submissions. Added pytest unit tests and used Git/GitHub for debugging and feature development.
